title: Vindictus

anticheat.note: anti-cheat present; it runs on Linux through Proton, which does not settle macOS

provenance: Reported by Yeetmaster on KLYC-Box's Discord (2026-09-30): on the Wine 11 engine (x64-crossover26.3) with DXMT the Steam connector opens and a server can be chosen, on the default engine it runs with no window. Measured on an M4 with macOS 27.0 on 2026-10-01 up to the connector's Nexon sign-in screen, on engines r15 and r12. The game itself was not played by the maintainer.
notes: Vindictus starts through Nexon's Steam connector (nxsteam.exe), a small Electron app that asks for a Nexon account and a server before the game opens. KLYC-Box adds Chromium's --in-process-gpu switch when you press Play, which makes the connector's window appear on the default engine. Measured here up to the Nexon sign-in screen only, the game past it is the reporter's.

knownIssues.symptom: Nothing appears after pressing Play on the default engine. Nexon's Steam connector runs in the background with no window
knownIssues.cause: The connector is an Electron app. Its separate GPU process draws into a window the main process owns, and Wine 10 cannot present across processes like that, so the window stays transparent (the Wine 11 engine carries a patch for it). Measured on an M4 with macOS 27.0 on 2026-10-01: invisible on engine r15, visible on r12, visible on both with --in-process-gpu
knownIssues.fix: KLYC-Box adds --in-process-gpu to the launch, which keeps the drawing inside the connector's own process. When starting from Steam's own window instead, put --in-process-gpu in the game's launch options (right-click Vindictus in Steam, Properties)
